name: Artix 7 FPGA logic fabric
summary: An executable LUT6, two FDRE-style registers, four carry stages, and a route mux inside an expandable FPGA resource map. This is a configured teaching network, not a complete CLB, bitstream loader, or full-device simulator.

groups.label: Configured logic fabric
groups.description: Representative primitive network. The selected function and number of cells are this example's design choices, not the device's resource count.

groups.label: LUT6 configuration
groups.description: Six address inputs select one of 64 configured bits. The example INIT implements parity.

groups.label: Clocked register stages
groups.description: Two rising-edge registers with common clock enable and synchronous reset; simultaneous updates preserve pipeline latency.

groups.label: Four-stage carry chain
groups.description: CARRY4 functional relationships. I0-I3 are used as S[0:3]; DI inputs are independent carry-generate selections.

groups.label: Selectable output route
groups.description: An explicit teaching mux chooses the combinational LUT result or first registered result.

groups.label: Device configuration
groups.description: LUT configuration bits are part of the JSON specification. Loading a real vendor bitstream is not implemented.

groups.label: BRAM and DSP resources
groups.description: Family-level resources shown as unexecuted boundaries; capacities depend on a selected SKU.

groups.label: I/O and clock context
groups.description: Package I/O and physical clock distribution are distinct from the lab's ideal Boolean signals.

inputs.label: I0 / S0
inputs.description: LUT address bit 0, the least significant bit. Also drives carry-select bit 0 in this example.

inputs.label: I1 / S1
inputs.description: LUT address bit 1 and example carry-select bit 1.

inputs.label: I2 / S2
inputs.description: LUT address bit 2 and example carry-select bit 2.

inputs.label: I3 / S3
inputs.description: LUT address bit 3 and example carry-select bit 3.

inputs.label: I5
inputs.description: LUT address bit 5, the highest address bit of this LUT6.

inputs.label: Register clock
inputs.description: An ideal positive-edge clock input. Use vector steps to distinguish levels from edges.

inputs.label: Clock enable
inputs.description: Capture data on a rising clock edge when CE is high and reset is low.

inputs.label: Synchronous reset
inputs.description: At a rising edge, reset overrides clock enable. Asserting it without an edge does not clear the FDRE-style registers.

inputs.label: Use registered output
inputs.description: Teaching route selection. This is not a runtime write to a real Artix routing bitstream.

inputs.label: Carry input CI
inputs.description: Carry input from a preceding carry-chain block.

inputs.label: Carry initialization
inputs.description: CARRY4 starts with CI OR CYINIT.

inputs.label: Carry data DI0
inputs.description: Carry-generate selection for stage 0 when S0 is low.

inputs.label: Carry data DI1
inputs.description: Carry-generate selection for stage 1 when S1 is low.

inputs.label: Carry data DI2
inputs.description: Carry-generate selection for stage 2 when S2 is low.

inputs.label: Carry data DI3
inputs.description: Carry-generate selection for stage 3 when S3 is low.

blocks.label: Configured LUT6
blocks.description: Six-input parity configured by the example INIT (0x6996966996696996 in MSB-first hexadecimal notation). The JSON stores address-zero first. Different contents create a different logic function, not a different hardware primitive.

blocks.label: FDRE register 0
blocks.description: Positive edge, INIT=0, no pin inversion. Synchronous reset has priority over CE; CE low holds the old value.

blocks.label: FDRE register 1
blocks.description: A second illustrative register samples the previous q0 on the same edge, demonstrating simultaneous commit rather than software statement order.

blocks.label: Output route mux
blocks.description: Select the first register or bypass it with the LUT result. The connection is authored for this example, not a claimed device routing netlist.

blocks.label: Initial carry
blocks.description: The functional initial carry is CI OR CYINIT.

blocks.label: Carry stage 0
blocks.description: S0 selects between the incoming carry and DI0.

blocks.label: Carry stage 1
blocks.description: S1 selects between CO0 and DI1.

blocks.label: Carry stage 2
blocks.description: S2 selects between CO1 and DI2.

blocks.label: Carry stage 3
blocks.description: S3 selects between CO2 and DI3; this is the chain's final carry.

blocks.label: Carry XOR output 0
blocks.description: O0 is S0 XOR initial carry, not S0 XOR CO0.

blocks.label: Carry XOR output 1
blocks.description: O1 is S1 XOR the incoming CO0.

blocks.label: Carry XOR output 2
blocks.description: O2 is S2 XOR the incoming CO1.

blocks.label: Carry XOR output 3
blocks.description: O3 is S3 XOR the incoming CO2.

requirements.text: The configured LUT returns INIT at the six-bit address with I0 least significant; the selected INIT implements parity.
Rising edges sample data with CE; CE low holds state and synchronous reset overrides CE without acting asynchronously.
The example mux selects either q0 or the combinational LUT result as configured by the route input.
Each carry stage selects its incoming carry when S is true or DI otherwise; XOR outputs use incoming carry.

assumptions: Positive-edge, non-inverted FDRE-style operation with INIT=0 is selected. Both registers share ideal clk, ce, and reset inputs.
The LUT6 configuration and route mux are authored teaching-design choices, not fixed functions of an unconfigured FPGA.
Functional primitive equations are checked against a fingerprinted open-source implementation, not against vendor simulation binaries.
No exact Artix 7 SKU, package, resource inventory, or physical slice arrangement is selected.
omissions: HDL elaboration, synthesis, routing-bit generation, configuration loading, timing analysis, propagation delays, setup/hold checks, and metastability.
BRAM/DSP arithmetic and port semantics, high-impedance Z, drive-strength/contention, PLLs, I/O voltages, and clock-domain crossing.
This is a small configured network, not all resources in a CLB/slice, a full FPGA, or a substitute for a hardware design tool.
